title: Private, public and holding companies
summary: The private limited company, its registration process, the public limited company, and holding and subsidiary companies: capital, members, shares and funding.

chunks.heading: Private limited company
chunks.explanation_md:
A **private limited company** keeps its funding close.

- **Funding**: it prohibits any invitation to the public to subscribe for shares, debentures or deposits from anyone other than its members, directors or their relatives.
- **Capital and members**: minimum paid up capital of **one lakh rupees** (or higher as prescribed, and by its articles), with **two to two hundred shareholders**.
- **Name**: must end with the suffix **Pvt. Ltd**.
- **Shares**: not traded in the open market, held only by directors and company members.
- **Liability**: limited to the extent of the shareholders' investment.
- **Starting**: needs the **Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association and Certificate of Incorporation** to commence business.

key_terms.meaning: No public invitation for shares; minimum paid up capital one lakh rupees; two to two hundred shareholders; name ends Pvt. Ltd; liability limited to investment.

chunks.exam_line: Private ltd: min paid-up capital one lakh rupees, two to two hundred shareholders, suffix Pvt. Ltd, shares not traded in open market, limited liability.

chunks.heading: Registration process of a Pvt. Ltd. company
chunks.explanation_md:
The slide is a picture titled **The Registration Process of a Pvt. Ltd. Company**, drawn as a winding path with these steps:

- Apply for the **DSC** (Digital Signature Certificate)
- Apply for the **DIN** (Director Identification Number)
- **Check for name availability** and implement it
- File **eMoA** (e-Memorandum of Association) and **eAoA** (e-Articles of Association)
- Apply for the **PAN and TAN** of the company
- Submit the certificate issued by the **ROC** (Registrar of Companies)
- **Open a current bank account** for the company

chunks.heading: Public limited company
chunks.explanation_md:
A **public limited company** raises funds from the public.

- **Capital**: minimum paid-up capital of **five lakh rupees**.
- **Members**: minimum of **seven**, with no maximum.
- **Shares**: traded in the open market on the stock exchanges where it is listed; easily transferable. It can raise part of its capital through a **public offering**, and invite people to subscribe for shares and debentures.
- **Being taken over**: it can be taken over by another company buying a controlling interest.
- **Prospectus**: must issue a prospectus before raising capital, and allot shares within **120 days** of the issue of the prospectus.
- **Name**: uses the suffix **Limited**.
- **Starting**: can start business only after the **certificate of commencement** from the Registrar of Companies.

key_terms.meaning: Minimum five lakh rupees paid-up capital, minimum seven members, shares traded on stock exchanges, prospectus required, suffix Limited.

chunks.heading: Holding and subsidiary companies
chunks.explanation_md:
A **holding company** either controls the composition of the board of directors of another company, or holds **more than half of the nominal value of the equity share capital** of another company.

The company that is controlled is the **subsidiary company**. A company is a subsidiary if its board is controlled by another company, which has the majority of the voting rights or the maximum number of shares needed for control.

key_terms.meaning: A company that controls another company's board or holds more than half of its nominal equity share capital.

questions.stem: What is a holding company, and what is a subsidiary?
questions.model_answer_md:
A **holding company** controls the composition of the board of directors of another company, or holds more than half of the nominal value of its equity share capital.

The controlled company is the **subsidiary**. It is a subsidiary because its board is controlled by the other company, which has the majority of voting rights or the maximum number of shares needed for control.

questions.stem: Differentiate a private limited company from a public limited company on capital, members, shares, funding and starting business.
questions.model_answer_md:
Both are joint stock companies with limited liability, but they raise money and start business differently.

| Basis | Private limited | Public limited |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum paid up capital | One lakh rupees | Five lakh rupees |
| Members | Two to two hundred shareholders | Minimum seven, no maximum |
| Name | Ends with Pvt. Ltd | Uses Limited |
| Shares | Not traded in the open market; held by directors and members | Traded on stock exchanges where listed; easily transferable |
| Funding | No invitation to the public for shares, debentures or deposits | Can raise part of capital by public offering; invites subscriptions |
| Prospectus | Not mentioned | Required before raising capital; shares allotted within 120 days |
| Being taken over | Not mentioned | Can be taken over by buying a controlling interest |
| Starting business | Can commence immediately after incorporation | Needs a certificate of commencement from the Registrar |

**Common ground.** Shareholder liability is limited to their investment; both are incorporated with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and a Certificate of Incorporation.

In conclusion, a private company stays closed and simple, while a public company trades openness for access to public funds.

questions.stem: Explain the stages in forming and funding a private limited company, using the registration process in the deck, and say how holding and subsidiary relationships arise between companies.
questions.model_answer_md:
A **private limited company** is formed through a registration process and funded by its members.

**Registration.** The picture shows: DSC, DIN, name availability check, filing eMoA and eAoA, PAN and TAN, the Registrar of Companies certificate, and opening a current bank account. It then holds the Memorandum, Articles and Certificate of Incorporation needed to commence business, and may commence immediately after incorporation.

**Funding.** It cannot invite the public for shares, debentures or deposits. Capital comes from members, directors or their relatives, with minimum paid up capital of one lakh rupees and two to two hundred shareholders. Shareholder liability is limited to their investment.

**Holding and subsidiary.** One company becomes a **holding company** when it controls the board of another company or holds more than half of its nominal equity share capital. The controlled company is the **subsidiary**.

In conclusion, the private company is set up by a clear registration path and funded from a closed group.
